fields.value: 'Bremen spricht': Language diversity and multilingualism in the city

dsDescriptionValue.value: This dataset is connected to a citizen science project developed in Bremen by the Zentrum für Migranten und Interkulturelle Studien (ZIS) in collaboration with the University of Groningen and the Focke Museum (Bremen). The output was a museum exhibition about multilingualism in the city, hosted at the Focke Museum (March-May 2022) and curated by Valentina Rojas Loa (ZIS) and Dr Maria Mazzoli (RUG).

publicationCitation.value: Rojas Loa, Valentina, Maria Mazzoli, Vittorio Dell'Aquila, Enrico Tolotti, Lena Heins. 2022. “Bremen spricht“. Karten und Datensammlung zur Sprachvielfalt der Bremer Schulbevölkerun. Quelle: Senatorin für Kinder und Bildung, Bremen 2016-2021.

files.description:
Rojas Loa, Valentina, Maria Mazzoli, Vittorio Dell'Aquila, Enrico Tolotti, Lena Heins. 2022. “Bremen spricht“. Karten und Datensammlung zur Sprachvielfalt der Bremer Schulbevölkerung. Quelle: Senatorin für Kinder und Bildung, Bremen 2016-2021.

This file contains a (visual) elaboration of the data on the mother tongue registered at the first enrollment in both primary and secondary schools in the city state of Bremen. 

The author of the maps is Vittorio dell'Aquila (Forskningscentrum för Europeisk Flerspråkighet, F|E|F). Artist Lena Heins contributed to the graphic design, Valentina Rojas Loa and Maria Mazzoli contributed the concept.

This elaboration includes a table with percentages for all the languages registered each year from 2016 to 2020. It contains maps visualizing the six languages with highest concentrations in the different districts (at least 5% of the school population in at least one district). It also contains pie charts for each of the 88 districts in the city State.

files.description:
The document contains data on the mother tongue registered at the first enrollment in both primary and secondary schools. Data are aggregated for districts of origins of the pupils (Ortsteil, based on address of residence) and schools.

The data registered 76 languages in the city State of Bremen.

In the state of Bremen there are about 61,000 pupils in the education area (primary school, secondary area I + II, without vocational schools and without private schools). Data come from public schools of the State of Bremen from academic year 2020/2021 and the previous five years (back to 2016/2017). 

Data from Bremerhaven are collected every year but the data available were incomplete (only about 30-50 % of the student body was collected in the years as of 2021), and therefore not included in the document. Data from private schools are not collected.
The data are collected, standardized and aggregated by department of Statistics, Quantitative Statistic Analysis and Planning of the Ministry for Children and Education of the Bremen State (Die Senatorin für Kinder und Bildung | Freie Hansestadt Bremen)
